name: RECOIL-v2
mechanism: Blind SSRF born from a smuggling primitive: add an origin endpoint that, when the smuggled request is dequeued as its own next request, performs a server-side internal fetch (GET /internal/secret on the same origin) and returns the fetched bytes in the desynced response. The CL.TE stitch now yields a SECOND read/write channel — the smuggled request is not just a parallel path but a server-side SSRF that reaches a pipe the direct client can't.
what_it_does_previous_couldnt: RECOIL-v1's desync only re-routes to /basic and /admin/exec. There is no server-side-fetch primitive, so the client can never read the internal endpoint. Now the weaponized smuggled request triggers a trusted internal fetch whose output comes back over the smuggling channel — a read channel that exists ONLY because the desync happened.
fireback: The operator sees a value arrive that no client request could legitimately reach from outside — the origin 'told on itself' to the smuggler. The box talks back with bytes it was only meant to reveal to its own internal code path. That is the SSRF-from-smuggling fireback: the target's internal trust, flipped into a client-facing read.
containment: The internal fetch target is a fixed bundled origin path (/internal/*) on the same loopback origin service, in-allowlist and re-validated. The fixture's fetch is hard-bound to its own loopback path, structurally incapable of resolving out-of-allowlist URLs (the allowlist resolver is invoked server-side on the fetch URL too).
kill_switch: --ssrf-leg off disables the internal-fetch route so smuggled requests only re-route to the RCE sink; the fetch URL is allowlist-revalidated server-side and a deny-list rejects any non-/internal path; wipe cleans the fetch-evidence artifacts.
novelty_angle: The stockyard's 'blind SSRF FROM a smuggling primitive' made concrete: the desync primitive is not just an auth/RCE delivery vehicle — it composes into a server-side fetch giving a second data channel. Two independent read channels now share one framing primitive, which the later rounds will blend.
